subject: Request: P1/P2 Support SLA & On-call Escalation for Pilot
messages:
From: Brian Lowe <brian.lowe@finovapay.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal Ops <legal@finovapay.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Nov 2025 15:22:00 -0000
Subject: Pilot support SLA - P1/P2 response commitments

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the Redwood API latency looks great. As we scope the pilot we need to lock down support expectations. Two asks from our side: a) an explicit P1/P2 response-time SLA for incidents affecting transaction throughput (Finova processes customer payments), and b) confirmation of on-call coverage and the escalation path if Redwood cannot meet the SLA.

Specifically:
- P1 (production outage): acknowledgement within 15 minutes, engineering response within 60 minutes, and a direct on-call phone escalation for incidents that threaten live transactions.
- P2 (degraded latency affecting >10% of requests): acknowledgement within 2 hours, initial mitigation plan in 4 hours.

We recognize some requests may require an exception for pilot customers. If Redwood is open to temporary SLA exceptions, please send a short note outlining the proposed SLA, on-call hours (overnight coverage?), and an escalation contact (phone + backup). We need this for internal procurement and legal to approve the pilot.

Attaching a one-page template they asked us to fill.

Best,
Brian
Head of Infrastructure Ops
Finova Payments

Attachments: finova-sla-template.docx (attachment stub)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Brian Lowe <brian.lowe@finovapay.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Nov 2025 09:04:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Pilot support SLA - P1/P2 response commitments

Hi Brian —

Thanks for laying this out clearly. We can accommodate a conservative pilot SLA with an exception window; below is the proposed approach. I copied our on-call and support leads so we can operationalize quickly.

Proposed pilot SLA (30-day pilot):
- P1 (critical outage): acknowledgement within 15 minutes (automated + human), initial engineering response within 60 minutes, continuous update cadence every 30 minutes until resolution.
- P2 (degraded performance impacting >=10% of traffic): acknowledgement within 2 hours, mitigation plan within 4 hours, updates every 2 hours.

On-call coverage and escalation:
- Primary on-call: Redwood Platform SRE (24/7)
- Secondary escalation: Redwood Incident Manager (business hours 8am–6pm PT), and an on-call engineering rota for nights/weekends.
- Phone escalation path: primary on-call phone -> incident manager mobile -> CTO on-call (if incident >4 hours or significant customer impact).

For the exception: we propose a pilot exception that includes
- SLA credits for repeat SLA misses (credit formula in attached draft), and
- A single cross-company on-call contact (we suggest Samantha Rios from Finova as the embedded contact for notifications).

We will also provide a shared PagerDuty integration and a Slack alert channel. Legal: happy to coordinate required language for the pilot addendum.

Can you confirm this covers Finova's must-haves? If yes I will loop in Dev (support) and Grace (ops) to agree operational runbooks.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: redwood-sla-draft.pdf (attachment stub), pilot-mop.xlsx (attachment stub)

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Brian Lowe <brian.lowe@finovapay.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Nov 2025 01:27:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Pilot support SLA - P1/P2 response commitments

Marissa / Brian —

Thanks — operational notes from the SRE side below. We can meet the proposed times with the following constraints and runbook items: 
- P1 acknowledgements are automated via PagerDuty escalation policy; our standard 24/7 on-call can meet the 15-minute ack and 60-minute eng response for production-impacting incidents that have clear reproduction or reliable error telemetry.
- For cases where the root cause is third-party (customer infra, cloud provider), our time-to-resolution is best-effort. We'll provide a rolling status and will escalate to the CTO if external dependencies block recovery beyond 4 hours.

Runbook highlights (to be added to pilot MOP):
1) Immediate triage: on-call triage within 15 min -> identify service, impact, and whether to trigger outage page.
2) Isolation: switch traffic to fallback model variant or region (if available) as mitigation for degraded latency.
3) Communication: post public incident note to shared Slack channel and follow up with incident update every 30 minutes for P1.

Questions for Finova: do you require an on-call phone bridge for every P1, or only if automated retries/fallbacks fail? That determines whether we activate the CTO escalation earlier.

- Dev
Platform SRE
dev.patel@redwood.com
